{
  "version": 1,
  "public": {
    "invalid_input": {
      "status": 400,
      "class": "validation",
      "retry": "never",
      "message": "Text must contain 1–1000 characters and no extra fields.",
      "remediation": "Check the input and try again."
    },
    "invalid_json": {
      "status": 400,
      "class": "validation",
      "retry": "never",
      "message": "Request body must be valid JSON.",
      "remediation": "Send a valid JSON body."
    },
    "writes_disabled": {
      "status": 403,
      "class": "forbidden",
      "retry": "never",
      "message": "Writes are disabled in this environment.",
      "remediation": "Use an environment that explicitly permits writes."
    },
    "not_found": {
      "status": 404,
      "class": "not_found",
      "retry": "never",
      "message": "Note, route or selected feature not found.",
      "remediation": "Check the target identifier and selected features."
    },
    "unavailable": {
      "status": 503,
      "class": "transient",
      "retry": "owner_only",
      "message": "The service is unavailable.",
      "remediation": "Check the previous operation's outcome before retrying."
    },
    "cancelled": {
      "status": 499,
      "class": "cancelled",
      "retry": "never",
      "message": "The operation was cancelled.",
      "remediation": "Start a new operation only when requested."
    },
    "internal_error": {
      "status": 500,
      "class": "unknown",
      "retry": "owner_only",
      "message": "The operation could not be completed.",
      "remediation": "Investigate the diagnostic identifier; verify writes before retrying."
    },
    "counter_limit": {
      "status": 409,
      "class": "validation",
      "retry": "never",
      "message": "The counter has reached its limit. Reset it to continue.",
      "remediation": "Reset the counter before incrementing again."
    }
  },
  "internal": {
    "input_invalid": "invalid_input",
    "request_json_invalid": "invalid_json",
    "write_forbidden": "writes_disabled",
    "resource_missing": "not_found",
    "storage_failed": "internal_error",
    "response_invalid": "internal_error",
    "network_failed": "unavailable",
    "ipc_failed": "unavailable",
    "export_failed": "internal_error",
    "state_unavailable": "unavailable",
    "clock_invalid": "internal_error",
    "unexpected_failure": "internal_error",
    "operation_cancelled": "cancelled",
    "counter_limit": "counter_limit"
  }
}

# Native counter

The Desktop counter starts at zero. Increment and reset operate on a mutex-protected Rust value, and renderer refresh reads that same value. App exit clears the in-memory counter. The notes sample and its save destination remain independent.

The renderer accepts only validated unsigned 32-bit integers. Native overflow returns the generated counter-limit policy without changing state; the UI preserves the last confirmed value and can read the current value before retrying. Three named IPC commands and their individual capabilities provide read, increment and reset; no setter or filesystem path is accepted.

Official documentation reviewed on 2026-10-12: [Tauri commands](https://v2.tauri.app/develop/calling-rust/), [Tauri state management](https://v2.tauri.app/develop/state-management/), and [embedded WebdriverIO plugin setup](https://webdriver.io/docs/desktop-testing/tauri/plugin-setup). The generated manifest pins Tauri Rust/API 2.12.2, CLI 2.12.1, React 19.3.0 and WDIO Tauri service/plugins 1.5.0. No SDK update is needed. Unit tests validate payload/failure handling and UI recovery; Rust tests cover reset, overflow and concurrent increments; native tests exercise the real renderer and Rust state on each required OS. Standard native release isolation remains required.
